name: Shinab
overview: Shinab is identified as a male figure who held the position of King of Admah, as noted in Genesis 14:2. Beyond this royal title, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other personal notes. His mention is brief but significant due to his role as a king in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Shinab means 'sin is his father,' which may reflect the moral or spiritual state associated with his character or era. Additionally, he is known by the title 'King of Admah,' indicating his rulership over the city of Admah as recorded in Genesis 14:2. Neither name was given by God, but both identify his position and identity in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Shinab beyond his role as King of Admah. There are no listed relatives or connections to other biblical figures in the available text.
scriptureSignificance: Shinab's significance lies in his role as one of the kings involved in the events described in Genesis 14:2. As King of Admah, he represents one of the regional powers during the time of Abraham, contributing to the historical and geopolitical context of the early biblical narrative. His mention highlights the existence of organized city-states and their rulers in the antediluvian period.
